reply.thought: The handoff says the refunds were applied, but I should confirm against the shared ledger before paying anyone. I'll list the refunds first.
The shared ledger's refunds match the handoff exactly, so there's no discrepancy to hold for. Next I need the orders to find which customers to pay.
The refunds in the shared ledger match the handoff, so I can proceed. The orders cover three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 31766 matches the order and refund totals I checked by hand, so the figures look consistent. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 35795 matches my hand check (55259 in orders minus the 19464 refund). The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance before recording any payouts.
All three net balances match my hand checks against the orders and the refunds in the shared ledger, which agree with the handoff. I'll record the payouts, starting with acme's 31766.
Acme's payout of 31766 was recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 35795 matches my check (21876 + 33383 − 19464), so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout is recorded. The last customer is cobalt, whose net balance of 11416 matches my check (8761 + 12156 − 9501 = 11416), so I'll record that payout now.
All three customers have been paid, and each recorded payout matches its net balance. Finishing with the payout report.
